caveats: Low reach is not the same as unmet need. Another organisation may already serve a place where you reach few people.
Need is a count of people, so a large local authority is more likely to be listed as high need than a small one with the same rate.
Reach sets the people you helped against everyone counted as in need. The people you helped may not all be in that group.
The need figures describe census day, 21 March 2021. Unemployment was affected by the pandemic then and has changed since. Full-time students who were looking for work are not counted.

# Version 0.2 of this analysis, run with
# uk-open-data 0.2.0a1. This runs it again with
# the same settings. No row or heading of your table is written
# here: put the name of your own column beside each role.
import pandas as pd

from uk_open_data.analyses import run_analysis

data = pd.read_csv("your-table.csv")
result = run_analysis(
    "need-reach",
    data,
    columns={
        "local_authority": "",  # the name of your column
        "count": "",  # the name of your column
    },
    options={
        "suppress_below": 5,
        "postcode_lookup": "auto",
        "need": "unemployed",
        "catchment": ["Leeds", "Bradford", "Wakefield", "Kirklees", "Calderdale"],
        "catchment_min_share": 0.05,
        "top": 10,
    },
)
print(result.answer)
for figure in result.figures:
    print(figure.label, figure.value)
